statement: Managers create a request for quotation, pick vendors and channels, preview the message, track vendor states, compare quotes and award; no message is sent without the manager's confirmation.

title: Service management 2.6.3: public vendor quote page and per-vendor verification-code switch
statement: The vendor page in RFQ mode shows the request, lets the vendor quote, update, withdraw, decline or ask, never reveals other vendors, counts "opened" only after the optional code, and a code the directory demands cannot be lowered.

title: Service management 2.6.3: map element on a request (migration 0090)
statement: A camera, device or Plan Studio object can be attached to a request from the live map, a camera page or the request picker; the vendor page shows a 2D floor picture with the element marked, or the text only when the element left the map.

title: Service management 2.6.3: optional WhatsApp number verification by a one-time code (migration 0091)
statement: Number verification by a one-time code is optional and off by default; a number counts as confirmed only after the code was typed back; the manager "I am sure" mark is allowed only while verification is off for the row and, for staff, needs the system-administrator permission and never overrides the person's own switch.

title: Arx 2.6.3: secrets moved from add-on options to Settings > Connections > Secrets (migration 0093)
statement: The go2rtc API password, WisKey password and background token, OpenAI key and push relay key are stored encrypted, set / replaced / cleared by a system administrator with a connection test for go2rtc and WisKey; no screen or log shows a value; the NVR password option is removed; deprecated empty options survive for one version and are imported and emptied at first start.

title: Service management 2.6.3: removal of the numeric quick-reply line from saved message templates (migration 0092)
statement: The numeric quick-reply line is gone from the starter texts and, by migration 0092, from templates an installation saved (he / en / ar / ru); running the statement again changes nothing.

title: Frigate 2.6.3: live video through Frigate's restream, events polling, NVR system card fix
statement: Frigate cameras with a matching restream stream live through Arx-owned smplwise_ streams (read-only toward Frigate; streams of other projects never touched), events stay fresh by polling when the live channel is quiet, and the NVR system card no longer asks a Frigate recorder (no 409).

title: Setup wizard 2.6.3: optional steps and a persistent per-user hint dismissal
statement: The floor and camera steps are optional, the "complete the installation" hint counts required steps only, and its dismissal is per user, survives a reload and can be restored.

title: Arx 2.6.3 release: combined service-management redesign, requests for quotation, map element, number verification, secrets, Frigate live video (integ/263)
statement: The combined 2.6.3 release (formerly 2.6.0 - 2.6.3) holds: contiguous migrations 0001..0093 that upgrade a populated 2.5.8 database, the user guide updated for every user-visible change, and the release notes; fakes and fixtures only.

title: Arx-only identities (CR-USR2): a second identity source behind security.local_identity
statement: Behind security.local_identity (off by default) a system administrator creates Arx-only users (one role at one scope, never system_admin), hands over a single-use first-login link, and those users sign in on the remote channel with a password stored only as a memory-hard hash; refusals are uniform, brute force is limited per account / address / installation, sessions are persistent, rotated and revocable, administrative permissions need the TOTP factor, administrative-target links are local-channel only; with the switch off nothing changes.

title: Arx-only identities on a real installation (tunnel, phone apps, host cost)
statement: The local sign-in works through the owner's Cloudflare tunnel, the session cookie survives phone-app restarts for its lifetime, and the password hash cost suits the owner's host.

title: Arx-only identities act in Home Assistant only through the service identity (USR2 P3)
statement: A local (Arx-only) principal's Home Assistant action runs as ONE configured non-administrator HA user, named with the person for attribution only, under a per-feature allow-list enforced by the add-on and the bridge; automations, doors, the area write and the stream source are refused; activity rows name the person; nothing changes while security.local_identity is off.

title: The service identity against the owner's Home Assistant
statement: With a real non-administrator service user configured on both sides, a local user's device, alarm, media, cast and schedule actions work and are attributed to the person.

title: External-person door grants on fakes (CR-ARX-WISKEY-SHARED-IDENTITY X1-X4)
statement: Arx links a contact to a WisKey person manually and issues time-bounded, approved, revocable door grants with a personal code by WhatsApp, under Arx RBAC; everything off and go-live not permitted in code.

title: External-person door grants on the owner's installation
statement: With the owner's separate go-live permit, a real grant works end to end on a WisKey station and a real phone, and is removed on revoke.

title: Arx-only people cannot reach through schedules what the extended-mode run fences forbid (Fable review 4, V-02)
statement: A schedule created, edited or run for an Arx-only (local) principal that runs a script or scene is bounded exactly like a direct run in the extended mode - both runnable allowlists and the bridge impact check under the service user's entity policy - or is refused; Home Assistant users are unaffected.

title: The extended mode refuses while the service user is not restricted by an entity policy - fail closed (Fable review 4, V-08; owner decision 3 of 2026-10-21)
statement: Every item only the extended mode admits is refused on both sides unless the service user is restricted (a group whose entity policy does not allow every entity, confirmed by Home Assistant's own permission object) and the add-on's report of it is current; an ambiguous or unreadable policy, a raising check or a stale report (Home Assistant unreachable) counts as not restricted; basic-mode items and Home Assistant users are unaffected.

title: Who is in the building (board r034) and the geofence / beacon / Wi-Fi editors on one screen (board r035)
statement: A holder of presence.view (sensitive, system_admin by default, scoped like the map) sees who the phone app currently places inside, by floor and area, on a screen that fits the viewport; only devices that acknowledged the current notice and report the sensor on count; an opted-out person is counted, never named or placed; every threshold is a setting; the geofences, beacons and Wi-Fi sites are edited on one settings page, network names kept as salted hashes only; nothing while presence is off (the default).

title: The release gate fails only on relevant tests
statement: Owner 2026-10-27: tests that are obsolete, duplicated or tied to a frozen / removed feature leave the gate, with each removal justified in a reviewable document; stale baselines are re-taken after review; the gate's reference counts match reality. Tests that guard security, permissions, data integrity, migrations, contracts or release_check are never removed.

title: WisKey A06 / T06 (W-031, board r152): identity source + role + scope -> admission, and the work-state mapping
statement: Every signed WisKey command is admitted only on the CURRENT Arx RBAC of the person it is attributed to (a revoke, expiry, delete or deny between two commands refuses the second); the emergency-open role given to non-administrators (EMROLE) admits the signed emergency command on its own scope only and lapses at use time; admitted / pending / running / accepted / active and a static status.active are never read as a sent door, a committed native write or a device proof.

title: External access to full scope: readiness check, graceful WisKey write path, service-writer adapter, one-time vendor code, visitor invitations (board r381)
statement: A system administrator sees, read-only and in plain Hebrew, which prerequisites of the external access are in place (write path, revoke proof, WhatsApp account, entrance stations, approvers) - unknown is never ok; grant writes never fail because WisKey's direct connection is selected: they use a service writer when WisKey offers one and otherwise fall back to the local service channel, with the reason shown; revokes are never blocked; a vendor's code can be a one-time code that is withdrawn after the first reported entry (best effort); a host with access.visitor.invite invites a visitor on the same grant engine (approval envelope routes, never refuses; no door code before the visitor's number is confirmed by code; entry log and a content-free arrival notice; 30-day erase); every switch stays OFF by default.

title: Door-window program written from Arx to WisKey (board r129)
statement: Arx writes each door's weekly hold-open program to WisKey only after validating it, proves every write by reading it back, never re-sends an unchanged program, records a version per proven write, detects a program changed or paused outside Arx and does not correct it automatically, retries a failed write a bounded number of times with a growing wait and then waits for a person, always lets the close direction (pause) through, shows the operator one plain Hebrew sentence per state, offers a dry run that writes nothing and a confirmed per-door write-again, and audits ids and codes only; nothing is live while the program engine build flag is off.

title: Security review 2026-10-27 (phone apps): the four medium findings fixed
statement: A route is exempt from the required-sensors policy only by an exact path match (non-canonical paths refused); a phone's device token and push registration end on every sign-out except a desktop-browser sign-out, and the event is audited; a device token on the remote channel obeys the user's remote-access policy; a valid device token is never refused by the failure limiter, and failures count per source address; a link that opens the app waits for the app lock and a link that asks for an action runs nothing without the user's confirmation.

title: A motion setting separate from the skin and the colour scheme
statement: The installation has a motion setting (automatic, full, reduced; default automatic) that is independent of the skin and the scheme: automatic follows the device's reduced-motion preference, full ignores it, reduced always removes motion; it is changed only with the permission to change the system look, is audited like the skin, and a corrupt stored value reads as automatic.

title: The emergency-buttons switch is an installation setting (owner q48)
statement: An administrator can switch the emergency buttons off and on for the whole installation (default on); the switch only gates the version's build approval and never starts the emergency engine; releasing an active incident never depends on it; every change is audited with who, when, before and after; turning it off needs an explicit confirmation and is refused while an emergency is active; the screen tells 'not approved in this version' apart from 'switched off'.

title: The live curved-wall browser checks are part of the release gate
statement: Every full release gate runs the two live curved-wall browser checks (curved walls and curved walls through points, desktop and phone) against the fake backend, so a change that breaks drawing, editing or showing curved walls stops the release instead of passing silently.

title: Security review 2026-10-27 follow-ups: the presence block on sockets, phone credentials end with a password change or a forced second factor
statement: A user blocked by the required-sensors policy (or the service identity) is refused on every WebSocket as on HTTP, with close 4403 and a reason frame; a password change or reset and a second factor made required for a user without one end that user's phone device tokens and push registrations, audited; an address with ?do=run only opens a confirmation; the Android link rules have JVM tests.

title: Reading an attached supplier certificate into proposals that a person decides field by field
statement: An administrator may switch document reading on (default off); a manager of a certificate or supplier-document task can have an attached text-layer PDF read into proposed supplier, document number, issue date, expiry date and scope values, each decided on its own; nothing changes the task, nothing leaves the add-on, no value reaches the audit, and drafts expire.

title: Supplier document reading: contiguous migration and the security review fixes
statement: The document-reading migration follows the release migrations without a gap or a clash; a crafted document cannot freeze the add-on (linear scrubbing, rules outside the write lock, bounded child output, bounded concurrent reads); proposals of deleted tasks do not linger.

title: Multi-Claude coordination protocol as documents and an optional tool
statement: The multi-Claude coordination protocol exists as optional documents and a tool; nothing in the product depends on it.

title: Proprietary all-rights-reserved licence notice; internal review notes untracked
statement: A proprietary all-rights-reserved licence notice is in the repository and 8 internal review notes under the gitignored private/ folder are no longer tracked.

title: Dependency, licence and secrets audit refreshed for v2.29.0
statement: docs/security/DEPENDENCY_AND_SECRETS_AUDIT.md is refreshed for v2.29.0 (inventory, licences, vulnerability and secrets scans) with findings H1, M1-M3, L1-L7 and the owner and counsel decisions recorded; the Heebo font licence text ships next to the UI fonts.

title: Task registry matched to the code history after 2.29.0
statement: management/tasks.json matches the code history after 2.29.0 (shipped tasks marked REVIEW, six train-3 cards added), views regenerated; no application test run.

title: The shared dialog keeps the keyboard focus inside its box
statement: sw-dialog traps Tab inside its box (aria-modal was declared without a trap).

title: Google Drive as an off-box backup target (device-flow OAuth, off by default)
statement: Google Drive is an off-box backup target kind: device-flow OAuth, drive.file scope, sealed tokens, off by default (migration 0186; design docs/design/GDRIVE_BACKUP.md). The owner's first real connection is NOT_RUN (see GDRIVE-READY-2351).

title: Dependency security fixes: Pillow 13, paramiko 5, format-restricted image decodes
statement: pillow 13.0.0 and paramiko 5.1.0 replace the vulnerable versions; untrusted image uploads decode only the expected formats and an MPO phone photo is accepted as its first frame (DEPAUDIT-2310 H1, M1, M2).

title: Worker dev tooling hardened; add-on base image pinned by digest (pin reverted in 2.31.1)
statement: Worker dev tooling is hardened and the add-on base image digests are pinned (DEPAUDIT-2310 M3, L2). The digest pin broke the Supervisor build and was reverted to the tag in 2.31.1 (see ADDON-IMAGE-BUILD-FIXES-2311).

title: Synoptic map and building cross-section read every home-system floor; floor mapping editor
statement: The synoptic map and the building cross-section read every floor of the home system: floors match by level on a one-building site, and a floor link editor links floors and adds or removes areas by hand (migration 0187).

title: Add-on image build fixes in 2.31.1 and 2.33.3
statement: The add-on image builds the way the Supervisor builds it: 2.31.1 references the base image by its tag again (the 2.31.0 digest pin made the build fail with "pip: not found"), 2.33.3 fixes the broken Dockerfile line of 2.33.2.

title: Public surfaces re-check before document links; module gate and CDN no-store on document answers
statement: Every public surface was re-checked and the result recorded; document links stop answering while service requests are off and are never cached by a CDN.

title: Report links: revoke on user deactivation, per-sender daily limit
statement: Every report link sent to a user is revoked when the user is deactivated or deleted; a per-sender daily limit for new links (default 50, a setting); the recipient name stays in the audit log (owner decisions 31.10).

title: Phone switch 44 px touch target and readable dark-mode muted text
statement: Phone switches have a 44 px tall touch target without changing their look; the secondary text in dark mode reaches at least 5:1 contrast in every skin.

title: Licence notice of the WisKey embed reference client (MIT) ships with the product
statement: The copyright and permission notice of the WisKey embed-api-v1 reference client (MIT) ships with the product.

title: Provision-ISR live and playback: video-only stream request, talk-back as a recorder setting
statement: On a Provision-ISR recorder go2rtc sources ask for video only (#backchannel=0) so live and playback show video; a recorder setting "two-way talk through the recorder" turns talk-back on, off by default.

title: A switch typed as a light counts and acts as lighting
statement: Switches set to the type "light" count as lights everywhere (synoptic map, home counters, floor and area cards) and are switched by "lights off / on".

title: Synoptic map hides columns without a data source; custom board columns
statement: Synoptic map columns with no data source are hidden (a setting, on by default, with a quiet note) and a custom column choice exists.

title: Calendars module switch reachable while the module is off
statement: Settings > Calendars stays reachable while the calendars module is off and the calendars page offers "enable the calendars module".

title: Multi-building home: site level, building cards, building switch, shared building
statement: On an installation of several buildings the home screen gets a site level (a card per building with counters and alerts, a grouped tree, a building switch, turn-off per building or for the site); a building can be marked as the shared building and is left unchecked by "turn off the whole site" (migration 0188; off until switched on).

title: Mapping assistant: which home-system name belongs to which building
statement: The assistant finds which home-system names belong to which building from a mark in the name, keeps a mark-to-building table, asks only about exceptions, applies the plan only after "Apply", keeps restorable versions (migration 0189).

title: External calendar connections: iCal subscription, Google Calendar, Microsoft 365 / Outlook
statement: An iCal subscription (read-only), Google Calendar or Microsoft 365 / Outlook can be bound to an Arx calendar; synchronisation runs only while the calendars module and calendar sync are on; outgoing iCal feeds are off by default and need their own switch (setup guide docs/operations/CALENDAR_CONNECT_SETUP.md). Real-provider connections are NOT_RUN.

title: No dimmer on on/off lights; switches in the synoptic lights column; floor lights popup
statement: Switches typed as a light and on/off-only lights show no brightness slider; a setting chooses which switches fill the synoptic lights column; pressing a floor's lights opens that floor's lights popup with "turn all on / off" through the usual confirmation.

title: Event centre polish (Security > Investigate > Events)
statement: The event centre side panel actions stay in view, the list scrolls in its own box, event names are Hebrew and technical details sit in a collapsible section; Up / Down move between events and Esc closes the panel.

title: Scroll arrows, wheel, swipe and keys for long tab strips
statement: Long tab strips scroll with arrows at their ends, the mouse wheel, a swipe and the keyboard (arrow keys, Home / End); a strip that fits looks as before.

title: Hide "ללא שיוך" from the building tree
statement: The unassigned row of the building tree can be hidden (always shown by default, only while editing, or never) from the home-screen options or on the row itself, with undo; counts do not change.

title: Provision-ISR live video steadier on a full wall of cameras
statement: Stream capabilities read from a Provision-ISR recorder are kept for ten minutes and shared, and when the recorder is briefly busy a tile opens on the stream the add-on already has instead of failing. The measurement on the owner's site is BLOCKED (no access; AZIA_LIVE_DIAG_2026-11-01_HE.md in private/).

title: The add-on recovers by itself after a crash during recorded-playback scrubbing
statement: A crash of the add-on server process restarts it within seconds, is recorded and shown in Diagnostics ("restarts after a crash"), leaves a full trace in the log, and after two crashes within six hours the server restarts on slower, steadier networking components for six quiet hours.

title: Owner answers of 01.11 (round 12): wording, unassigned section, tablet side panel
statement: The connections page and the setup guides no longer say Arx never writes to the recorder; the "ללא שיוך" choice also governs the unassigned section of the tiles view; the layout editor side panel is a bottom sheet on tablets as well as phones (answers 5A, 6A, 8B).

title: Three leftovers of the 2.33.1 polish round
statement: The three leftovers of the 2.33.1 design polish round are closed (see the change record).

title: Live video of H.265 cameras in browsers that cannot decode H.265
statement: For H.265 cameras in browsers that cannot decode H.265 the server picks a fallback (the camera's other H.264 stream, else an on-demand transcoded H.264 copy shared by viewers with a cap); the tile shows which stream it got and a Hebrew message when there is none.

title: Switch every camera stream to H.264 from the UI; per-recorder NVR writes switch
statement: A per-recorder switch "אפשר שינויי הגדרות ב־NVR" gates every setting write (Provision-ISR off by default, Hikvision unchanged) and the bulk encoding dialog has a one-click "convert every stream to H.264" preset. No write to a real recorder was run by the branch.

title: Shared-layer proposals of the design-polish round
statement: One technical-details disclosure, a common settings kit, centred empty states, a failure tone for media-page messages, opt-in content-sized dialogs and keyboard-focusable table rows.

title: Service requests: one compact toolbar for the list and the manager board
statement: The request list and the manager board share one compact toolbar with one Filter panel, removable chips, the view switch and "new" on the title row.

title: Service request settings and side screens polish
statement: Service request settings and side screens use one column below 1000 px, one save pattern per card and clearer loading and switched-off states.

title: Layout editor, device controls and automations screen polish
statement: The layout editor panel is grouped, device controls share one control look, a cover tilt sits apart from its position, and the automations screen loads with the shape of its list.

title: People and access administration polish (wave 1)
statement: User and group drawers are side panels (a bottom sheet on a phone), deny rules are marked in the tables and loading, error and empty states are consistent.

title: Calendars and messaging settings polish
statement: Calendar, calendar connections and messaging channel settings have no cut-off rows, behaviour settings are grouped by topic and card actions sit at the foot of each card.

title: Media and doors polish (wave 3)
statement: The players page fits the window with only its cards scrolling, the casting table lines up, door cards name each switch and the remote editor keeps save / cancel on screen.

title: WisKey stations and water pages polish (wave 3)
statement: The stations screen fits the window on a desktop, the water pages take the height under the tabs and the chart follows its box width.

title: Look and branding settings polish (wave 2, part A)
statement: The logo settings have keyboard-friendly tabs and an unsaved-changes mark and the wall-screen users list, empty state and drawer are reorganised into clear sections.

title: Camera administration polish (wave 3)
statement: The privacy masks editor fits the window on a wide screen and the multi-camera batch list and progress rows are clearer.

title: Automations and schedules administration polish (wave 3)
statement: Automation and schedule rows stack instead of squeezing in a narrow column, the slot panel and table view are tidier and the create dialog keeps its actions on screen.

title: Investigation leftovers polish (cases, one case, exports, event page)
statement: The cases list fits the window with status filters and a count, a case page has two scrolling columns, exports are grouped and the event page shows Hebrew event names.

title: Insights and infrastructure reports polish (wave 3)
statement: Insights and infrastructure reports have calmer counters, one segment track, openable door rows and larger touch targets on tablets and phones.

title: Home editing screens polish (wave 3)
statement: The home edit panel is grouped, widget rows are wells, keys and fields are 44 px on a phone and a triggered alarm shows on the phone ambient bar.

title: Setup and plan administration polish (wave 3)
statement: Connection results show as status lines with an icon and the map settings and area-links pages use the common settings look.

title: Tabs display settings polish (wave 2, part B)
statement: The tabs display settings have two headed groups, choices as tiles, one save / error line and a retry panel.

title: Smooth recorded playback under fast scrubbing
statement: Rapid seeks are merged (only the last is sent), each seek closes the old stream before opening the next, a per-minute seek cap (setting, default 30) shows a Hebrew notice, and timeline previews show the nearest available picture within 30 seconds.

title: The server runs on asyncio and h11 by default (uvloop and httptools opt-in)
statement: The server runs on the standard asyncio and h11 components by default (a suspected native crash source is off); a Diagnostics setting turns the fast components back on after a restart.

title: False "write gate held outside a transaction" log alarm removed
statement: The false "write gate held by events_ingest._write outside a transaction" alarm is gone and a camera-list read no longer takes the write lock.

title: Refused Frigate credentials: one health item instead of a flooded log
statement: Refused Frigate credentials no longer flood the log: Arx backs off up to 30 minutes, logs once per change and shows the exact fix step in Hebrew on the recorder health card.

title: Release gate proves the add-on image builds the way the Supervisor builds it
statement: Release checks validate the add-on build files (base image by tag, Dockerfile syntax, arch and labels), so a broken build like 2.31.0 or 2.33.2 is caught before release.

title: Accessibility pass over the screens polished on 31.10 and 01.11
statement: Escape closes popovers and only the top dialog, every form field has a screen-reader name, arrow keys work in tab rows, save results are announced and light-mode status text meets 4.5:1.

title: Dark-mode review of the screens polished on 01.11
statement: Five dark-mode contrast fixes on the polished screens and the selected segment of every segmented control is a raised, lighter key.

title: Faster home and devices screens: lazy screens, settings in two queries, shared requests
statement: Each screen loads on demand (home and devices open 33-44% faster), settings are read in 2 queries instead of hundreds and identical requests are shared.

title: The shared button is 44 px high on a phone
statement: The shared button is drawn at least 44 px high on a phone.

title: The synoptic map on phones in three layouts
statement: The synoptic map has three phone layouts (compact table by default, floor cards, building section) chosen in its settings, with no overlapping numbers.

title: Tickets table width at 1440 and 1280 px; settings tab duplication
statement: The tickets table fits 1440 and 1280 px without sideways scrolling and settings pages with their own tabs no longer repeat them in the sidebar.

title: Release gate fixes of 2.34.2 (groups A, B, C and the pixel side)
statement: The failures of the first 2.34.2 release gate are fixed (lazy-screen group, plan editor / camera card / tickets table / cross-section group, group C and the pixel baselines).

title: Outlook-style editing on the calendar grid
statement: Drag across free time to create (quick-create popover), drag an event to move it, drag its edge to resize, peek card, keyboard and long-press support and undo after move / resize / delete; moving an approved booking in an approval room becomes a request (per-calendar setting); editing by dragging can be limited to "create only" (migration 0191).

title: Named attendees of calendar entries
statement: Calendar entries have named attendees (Arx users, residents and external guests stored encrypted) with in-app notices, guest notices on the configured channel, RSVP, count-only privacy for viewers and settings per installation and per calendar (migration 0190). Guest messages to real recipients are NOT_RUN.

title: Reuse SQLite connections between requests
statement: Database connections are reused between requests (settings read 2.6x faster); the add-on option db_conn_pool turns it off.

title: Browser and backend evidence before the 2.35.0 gate
statement: The pre-gate runner check of the 2.35.0 train is run and its failures fixed (a11y skeleton spec, evidence-devices specs, compact density on area cards).

title: Release gate of 2.35.0: the six backend failures
statement: The six backend failures of the 2.35.0 gate are fixed (WAL scrub on its own connection with the pool, attendee module name, upload counters wait).

title: Building notice board with TV screens (CR-NOTICE106) and the 2.18.0 overhaul
statement: A building notice board with notices, audiences, push and TV boards exists (module off by default); the 2.18.0 overhaul adds the notices page parity with the approved mock-up, writing notices from the settings, status chips, promo / info slides and building photo, screen saver and logo layouts, a permanent TV link and push on publish.

title: Notice board follow-ups: news sources, deletion, TV options, removal fix, nearby bus times
statement: Editable news (RSS) sources and connection caps of the TV listener, real deletion of a notice, one-row header / "updated" line / weather forecast days options with installation-wide defaults, the "remove from board" fix and nearby bus times (a labelled estimate, off by default).

title: TV notice board V2 design and the owner answers of 27.10
statement: The notice board TV page follows the approved V2 mock-up (96 px header with the tenant and SmplWise logos, weather under the date, fixed bus area per layout); the "updated" line has two wordings (place and time - the default - or time and board name), an idle board can show the logos, and the one-row header survives very long names.

title: Lobby screen styles (Gallery, Concierge, Stone, Lumen, Axis, Prism, Ink and Sign)
statement: Three luxury lobby styles (Gallery, Concierge, Stone) with a day and a night building photo, three hi-tech styles (Lumen, Axis, Prism) and the Ink and Sign board styles for maintenance areas are selectable; nothing changes until an administrator chooses one.

title: Phone-app server side: saved sign-in, device key, WebView session exchange, attestation, critical sound
statement: The server supports the phone apps: persistent sign-in with a device key (APPREFRESH), the one-time-code WebView session exchange (POST /auth/app/session and /redeem), device attestation, offline field work (server half) and critical-sound alerts - every one off by default.

title: Push on publish for the notice board to the phone app channel
statement: Publishing a notice sends a push through the notification core's app channel (generic payload to the relay, text fetched by the app with its device token); it sends nothing until SW_PUSH_RELAY_URL and the key are set.

title: Worst-case data on the main screens: long names, empty states, huge counts, no scrolling
statement: Screens with extreme data stay in their cards: long area and cover names end in an ellipsis and keep their kind visible, five-digit counts widen their own row, temperatures and stale times give way last with the full value in a tooltip, the large weather widget shrinks its temperature to fit, the side rail active marker no longer counts as overflow.

title: Gate: runner entry check before a release train + 7-day quarantine list
statement: A runner entry check runs before any branch joins a release train, with a single quarantine list of at most 7 days.

title: Calendars UI: booking calendars, approvals, maintenance calendar, resident view, sync settings (owner answers 30.10)
statement: Calendars: month, week and day views, a rooms timeline, booking, approvals (contested requests; displacing needs the calendar manager), maintenance, calendar management, settings and connections and a resident flow on the phone; every owner decision is a setting (module off by default).

title: Temperature report: security review and hardening of the report link and WhatsApp send
statement: Temperature report links: separate switches for system users and for names in shared PDFs (off by default), revocation when a WhatsApp number changes, no caching of the link answer.

title: Phone layer polish: chips and switch hit areas
statement: Phone layer: 16 px fields (no zoom on focus), no tap flash, no sticky hover, press feedback, 44 px hit areas, phone type tiers, dropdowns and pop-ups inside the screen (dvh).

title: Presence card: compact redesign (owner rejected the tall card 30.10)
statement: The building presence card is a compact strip of active rooms (four styles; empty rooms, details and "empty since" are settings) never taller than its neighbours, and the area window shows the room status.

title: WisKey rc.4 adoption + rc.5 host check (deadline fix, migration 0186, relay-by-door fix)
statement: The WisKey rc.4 owner30 contribution and the rc.5 host check (one absolute deadline before the live wrapper selection, installed-client migration, a door relay is WisKey's physical relay in every station grant) are adopted on a branch with fakes only; auto-install stays off.

title: Python constraints lock file for the add-on

title: Supervisor build check with the lock file

title: Reboot one camera through its NVR (legacy parity P09)
statement: A holder of the sensitive permission nvr.camera.reboot (installation and camera scope) can reboot one camera from the camera's settings: Hikvision only (the legacy request GET /ISAPI/ContentMgmt/InputProxy/channels/{ch}/reboot through the NVR, one PUT only when the device proves the GET was not executed), refused while the NVR-writes switch is off, after a confirmation dialog, rate limited per camera and per user, recorded in the NVR change log and audited; Provision-ISR is refused as unsupported; the button is disabled with a plain reason when the permission is missing or NVR changes are off.

title: Recordings: month view of the days with recordings (legacy monthly calendar parity)
statement: The playback screen offers a month view beside the date field: the days of a local month (installation IANA zone) with any recording of the camera are marked, future days are disabled, a tapped day opens that day; Hebrew, RTL, no scrolling inside the card, phone bottom sheet. Backend GET /api/v1/cameras/{id}/recordings/days?month=YYYY-MM is read-only on the recorder (Hikvision dailyDistribution, fallback derived from the bounded recording search with honest partial coverage; Provision-ISR SearchRecordDate), uses the camera's own recorder (multi-NVR), is cached (60 s current month, 1 h past) and bounded, and never asks the device for a future month.
